themes.name: Integration of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) in Higher Education Curricula
themes.definition: The process of incorporating the UN's Sustainable Development Goals and Education for Sustainable Development into academic programs and courses within higher education institutions, often aimed at aligning with the 2030 Agenda and fostering societal transformation.
evidence: [CueInc_2024] Higher Education Institutions in their societal transformative role need to effectively integrate the UN‘s Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the 2030 Agenda into their curricula.
[DécSul_2017] This paper highlights the contribution of the Sulitest to the global agenda of integrating sustainability into higher education.

themes.name: Active and Problem-Based Learning Pedagogies for ESD
themes.definition: The use of participatory, hands-on teaching methods such as problem-based learning, active learning, and experiential learning to facilitate education for sustainable development, often emphasizing real-world applications and student-centered approaches.
evidence: [CarExp_2023] This study aims to explore the usefulness of problem-based learning (PBL) approaches to train biomedical students in sustainability.

[MarHig_2022] The purpose of this paper is to analyse which are the active learning methodologies, which had better contribute to acquiring competences for sustainable development (SD) in higher education.

themes.name: Development of Sustainability Competences and Capabilities
themes.definition: The acquisition and enhancement of specific skills, knowledge, and attitudes necessary for addressing sustainability challenges, including transverse competences like collaboration and critical thinking, as well as disciplinary competences.
evidence: [CueInc_2024] The participants strengthened both, transverse competences (collaboration, citizenship, communication, and critical thinking) and disciplinary competences (subject matter).

[ThoCon_2016] The reported research aims to examine the extent to which sustainability capabilities have been delivered by a specific example of Education for Sustainability (EfS) and Education for Sustainable Development (ESD).

themes.name: Interdisciplinary and Transdisciplinary Collaboration in ESD
themes.definition: Collaborative approaches that involve multiple disciplines, courses, or external stakeholders in education for sustainable development to address complex sustainability issues, often through partnerships with communities, NGOs, or industry.
evidence: [CueInc_2024] It also implemented horizontal (intraclass), vertical (interclass), and interdisciplinary (multiple courses) student collaboration.

[HilEdu_2022] The paper investigates how teacher trainees in higher education geography and external, non-scientific partners perceive and experience collaborations in an active teaching and learning approach.

themes.name: Institutional and Organizational Strategies for ESD Implementation
themes.definition: The policies, support structures, and strategic approaches at the institutional level to integrate and promote education for sustainable development within higher education, including faculty development, curriculum design, and whole institution approaches.
evidence: [DurMod_2026] The findings indicate that educators’ intentions are primarily driven by perceived behavioral control, self-efficacy, faculty development, interdisciplinary course design, and institutional support.

[TreStu_2023] It analyses students’ learning experiences in self-led sustainability projects conducted outside formal curricula to highlight their potential contribution to HESD in the sense of the whole institution approach.

themes.name: Student Engagement and Perspectives in ESD
themes.definition: The involvement, attitudes, beliefs, and experiences of students in education for sustainable development activities, including their views on sustainability integration in curricula and their future roles in the workplace.
evidence: [ChaThe_2023] This study aims to gain insight into IT students' perspectives on the role of education for sustainable development (ESD) in their academic curriculum.

[BalSus_2025] The aim of this study is to gauge the consideration toward sustainability and sustainable development in the creative process or activities in design practices among the design undergraduates.

themes.name: Teacher and Faculty Development for ESD
themes.definition: Training and professional development programs for educators to enhance their skills, knowledge, and competences in delivering education for sustainable development, often focusing on reorienting curricula and teaching methodologies.
evidence: [ExpImp_2020] The aim of this training course on professional education for sustainable development (ESD) skills and competences for higher education teachers is to help academics in reorienting their subjects' curricula.
[BraBec_2019] This paper aims to provide a holistic approach to assessing student teachers’ competence development in education for sustainable development (ESD).

data.meta_observations: The abstracts consistently emphasize the integration of SDGs and ESD into higher education, with a strong focus on pedagogical innovation, competency development, and collaborative approaches. Many studies employ mixed-methods research and highlight context-specific adaptations. There is a recurring theme of transformative learning aimed at fostering change agents for sustainability.
data.grounding_notes: Themes were derived inductively from verbatim text in the abstracts. Some themes overlap, such as 'Active and Problem-Based Learning Pedagogies' and 'Development of Sustainability Competences,' but were distinguished based on primary focus. All evidence quotes are exact from the provided abstracts, and article keys are strictly from the closed set. Confidence levels are assigned based on clarity and frequency of evidence in the batch.
